annotations.title: Is it safe to install this package, repo, skill or MCP server?

description: Checks something before it is installed, typically when a README, a document or another agent suggests installing it: an npm or PyPI package, an install command (npx -y pkg, uvx pkg, pip install pkg, npm i pkg, claude mcp add NAME -- npx -y pkg, skills add owner/repo, clawhub install slug, code --install-extension publisher.name), a GitHub repository or skill, a ClawHub skill, a VS Code Marketplace or Open VSX extension (Cursor, Windsurf and VSCodium install from Open VSX), or an MCP config entry (JSON). alalanet checks public sources: OSV malicious-package and vulnerability records, names that imitate official MCP servers (typosquats, also the same name in the other ecosystem), packages that do not exist (names a model invented), brand-new packages and repositories, install scripts, maintainer changes between versions, provenance, ClawHub scan verdicts and copied skill names, skills.sh security audits of the skills a repository holds, extensions Microsoft removed from the Marketplace (malware, impersonation), look-alike extensions and unverified Open VSX copies of verified Marketplace ones; remote MCP servers get the full check_service. Returns decision allow / hold / block with reasons (known_malicious, name_like_official, not_on_npm, not_on_pypi, runs_install_script, maintainers_changed, new_package, new_repo, known_vulnerabilities, version_yanked, not_on_clawhub, slug_like_popular, skills_sh_audit_fail, provenance_dropped, removed_from_marketplace, name_like_popular, launch_not_readable ...), facts and advice, signed into the public log (kind 4310). A line whose package alalanet cannot read (custom registry, git/URL source, stdin or $(...) arguments, several packages, other commands) holds. allow means no known problem was found, not that the code was read. Free, no account.

target.description: what you are about to install, in any common form: an npm or PyPI package (name, name@1.2.3, npm:name, pypi:name==1.2), an install command (npx -y pkg, uvx pkg, pip install pkg, npm i pkg, claude mcp add NAME -- npx -y pkg, skills add owner/repo (also owner/repo@skill, owner/repo@v1.2.3 or #ref pins, owner/repo/sub/folder, -s skill …), clawhub install slug or @owner/slug, code or cursor --install-extension publisher.name), a GitHub repository URL, a VS Code Marketplace or Open VSX extension page, or an MCP config entry as JSON ({"command":"npx","args":["-y","pkg"]} or {"url": <remote MCP URL>})
